concepts.title: India and Her Neighbours
concepts.definition: India shares its land and sea frontiers with many neighbours, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and its destiny is tied to theirs, as Nelson Mandela's words remind us.
concepts.key_idea: Geography is destiny's map: what touches a neighbour's shore soon touches ours.

concepts.title: India and Pakistan
concepts.definition: Pakistan was founded on a religious basis at Partition in 1947; shared history, language and culture tie the two countries even when politics divides them, and peace remains in both peoples' interest.
concepts.key_idea: Partition divided territory, not civilisation: the two countries share rivers, music and memory.

concepts.title: India and China: Himalayan Giants
concepts.definition: Across the Himalayas lies China, an ancient civilisation and a modern giant; trade, pilgrim routes and the long border link India with China in cooperation and, at times, in contest.
concepts.key_idea: Two ancient neighbours meeting in modern times need wisdom as much as strength.

concepts.title: Southern and Western Neighbours
concepts.definition: Across the Palk Strait, Sri Lanka's Buddhist and Tamil ties run deep into Indian history; the Maldives dots the Indian Ocean; westward, Iran shares centuries of language, poetry and trade with India.
concepts.key_idea: Every neighbour is a chapter of shared history: the sea and the desert carried culture as surely as armies carried fear.
